findings.F1: The book's edge is too small to survive its fees and its idle time. It is flat on Monday to Saturday and holds a short only from the Sunday close to the Monday close, with a mean absolute position of 0.43 on the 1,290 active Sundays. The gain per active Sunday is 0.000776 (t 1.01, 1,284 cases), and the fee on the same Sundays averages 0.000451. The book's mean daily return ends at -3.5e-06 against the 0.0005 required.
findings.F2: The weekend reversal itself is real. After an up Sunday, Monday returns -0.0046 and the Monday-Tuesday pair -0.0076. After a weekday up-day, the next day returns +0.0005 (t 0.87, 6,117 cases) and the next two days +0.0037. On active Sundays Monday returns -0.0044 (t -2.99) and Tuesday -0.0037 (t -2.78). Holding only Monday therefore leaves half of the fall unused.
findings.F3: The book's sizing runs against the shape of the rise side. Positions grow with the rise, but the smallest-forecast quartile had the largest Monday fall (-0.0079 at a mean position of -0.04). The largest quartile fell only -0.0043, at a mean position of -0.94. By Sunday z-score sextile, Monday-Tuesday returns are -0.0077/-0.0069 at z 0.25 and -0.0025/-0.0021 at z 1.84. This is why the step-5 large-minus-small check came out +0.0035.
findings.F4: The fall side, which the book never trades, reverses with a clear grading. Sundays in the lowest z sextile (mean z -1.63) are followed by Monday +0.0136 and Wednesday +0.0089. The next sextiles (z -0.58 and -0.13) are followed by Monday +0.0041 and +0.0005, while the average day returns +0.0012.
findings.F5: Trading both sides makes the effect hold across windows. A vol-scaled position opposite to the Sunday z, held Monday and Tuesday, earns 0.000264 per Sunday (t 2.65, 2,051 cases) and 0.000235 on Monday alone (t 2.83). The short-only version earns t 1.46 over two days, and the book's actual Monday short earns t 0.37. The two-sided version is positive in 62.5% of windows with a worst window mean of -0.0006. The actual book is positive in 37.5% of windows with a worst of -0.0042. By coin it is positive in 5 of 6 coins, strongest in XMR (t 2.56).
findings.F6: The relative weekend volume does not grade the Monday reversal. Monday returns are -0.0055, -0.0036 and -0.0047 across volume terciles. Even the two-sided two-day reversal is only about 0.00004 per calendar day, so it raises the Sharpe and window stability but cannot by itself reach a mean daily return of 0.0005.

ideas.idea: A coin that rose over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) falls over the next 2 days (Monday and Tuesday), and a coin that fell over the weekend rises over those 2 days. In both cases the larger the weekend move relative to the coin's usual daily move, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: The weekend move should be faded on both sides and held through Tuesday, which roughly doubles the usable reversal per fee paid compared with a Monday-only short.
ideas.name: weekend moves reverse both ways

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days, and the larger the weekend fall relative to its usual daily move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: Sharp weekend sell-offs are a reason to buy into Monday rather than to sell.
ideas.name: weekend falls rebound early-week
